diffs.diff: pin count: part has 13 (GND 3V3 SDA SCL INT AVDD RED/E+ BLK/E- WHT/A- GRN/A+ YLW/SD B- B+), datasheet reading has 4 (GND 3V3 SDA SCL)
diffs.evidence: The part models the SparkFun Qwiic Scale SEN-15242. Its hookup guide documents the I2C edge pins (GND, 3V3, SDA, SCL) plus an 'AVDD Pin' ('The NAU7802 has a built-in voltage regulator and will output 4.5V to 2.4V used to bias the load cell') and an interrupt/data-ready pin ('Interrupts / Data Ready ... the NAU7802 has an interrupt output pin'), and the PTH load-cell pins: 'Pin Definitions: Red/E+ ... Black/E- ... White/A- ... Green/A+ ... Yellow/Shield ... B- - Called VIN2N in the datasheet ... B+ - Called VIN2P in the datasheet.' That is 13 pins. The second reading listed only the 4 I2C/power pins and left out the INT, AVDD and load-cell pins that a load cell has to be wired to.

diffs.diff: differential input voltage (V, PGA gain 1, VREF=3.3V): datasheet reading gives 3.93392e-7 per count, the part's model has 0.000001397
diffs.evidence: NAU7802 datasheet rev 1.7, section 9.2: 'In normal operation the input signal is full scale at the ADC input when (VINxP - VINxN) = +/- 0.5 * (REFP - REFN) / PGA_Gain'. The full range is VREF/gain across the 24-bit two's-complement code range, so 1 LSB = VREF/(gain*2^24). At gain 1 and VREF 3.3 V that is 3.3/16777216 = 1.967e-7 V. The second reading's 3.934e-7 (= 3.3/2^23) assumes a +/-VREF full scale, which doubles the value and contradicts the datasheet. The model's 1.397e-6 is the simulator scale in mV per count at the driver's own setting (gain 128, LDO/VREF 3.0 V): 3.0/(128*2^24) = 1.397e-9 V = 1.397e-6 mV. That matches the datasheet formula and the driver's to_microvolts (raw*VREF*1e6/(gain*2^24)). The numbers differ only because of the units (mV vs V) and the gain/VREF condition. The example test agrees: 5 mV -> raw 3579139 = 5e-3*128*2^24/3.0.
